Document text extraction. Public text edition; layout and embedded images are not reproduced.

To Fine Spind, on the occasion of articles concerning KP22Web: www.computerlars.com Mail: [████] (1600 characters): ‘Computer Lars’ is an anagram of the author ‘Marcel Proust’. The anagram can, as shown in the portrait photo, partly deceive that Marcel Proust simply is Computer Lars, while in the works on KP Digital it expresses the reverse angle, namely Marcel Proust as seen by Computer Lars.
Computer Lars’ series of works on KP Digital is called “Variations sur le thème Marcel Proust,” with a reference to the system poet Georges Perec's rewritings of Proust. The works consist of a series of visual variations on Proust as viewed through a computer. The technique behind it is a neural network's text-to-image generation, and each of these images is titled with an anagrammatic pun on Proust. The whole is set up as a hypersystem where one can move across images, literary texts, and tools for current and historical computer art.
Theoretically, Computer Lars mirrors the genre ‘AI art,’ which mostly serves as a showcase for Big Tech, and often aims to demonstrate the capabilities of technology. Against this, Computer Lars unfolds the idiomatic of artificial stupidity, i.e., AI’s material and linguistic specificity. With Computer Lars, exhibiting AI-generated material becomes less a triumph for technology and more an illustration of the role of computation in art and literary history. Thus, one can discover immediately counterintuitive relationships, e.g., between the computer and Proust’s life, name, and work.
Previous activations of Computer Lars include a bookshelf in Mejlborg, an exhibition at Spanien19c, the magazine Monsieur Antipyrine, a digital novel, and a project with the tech company MindFuture.
